verses.text: I love the Lord because he hears my prayers and answers them.
Because he bends down and listens, I will pray as long as I breathe!
Death stared me in the face—I was frightened and sad.
How kind he is! How good he is! So merciful, this God of ours!
The Lord protects the simple and the childlike; I was facing death, and then he saved me.
Now I can relax. For the Lord has done this wonderful miracle for me.
He has saved me from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling.
I shall live! Yes, in his presence—here on earth!
In my discouragement I thought, “They are lying when they say I will recover.”

footnotes.text: In my discouragement I thought, “They are lying when they say I will recover,” literally, “I said in my alarm, all men are liars.”

verses.text: But now what can I offer Jehovah for all he has done for me?
I will bring him an offering of wine and praise his name for saving me.

footnotes.text: an offering of wine, literally, “the cup of salvation,” i.e., the thank offering of wine for saving me.

verses.text: I will publicly bring him the sacrifice I vowed I would.
His loved ones are very precious to him, and he does not lightly let them die.

footnotes.text: His loved ones are very precious to him, and he does not lightly let them die, literally, “Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.” See context for the validity of the paraphrase.

verses.text: O Lord, you have freed me from my bonds, and I will serve you forever.
I will worship you and offer you a sacrifice of thanksgiving.
Here in the courts of the Temple in Jerusalem, before all the people, I will pay everything I vowed to the Lord. Praise the Lord.
